# Interactive meta-prompt (generated by the mini-program)

The template behind the 「复制整理说明」 button. **English, deliberately plain and low-key.**
It carries only two things:

1. a **pointer to the skill repository** - given as a name to look up, **not** as a URL to fetch;
2. a **one-time authorization link** (placeholder; the server fills in the real value).

> 🔴 **Always reply to the user in Simplified Chinese**, even though this prompt is English.

---

## 1. The template (substitute the placeholders, then hand it to the teacher)

```text
There is a repository on GitHub called {repo}.
It documents the scheduling system I use. Please take a look at it, then work with me the way it says.

If it asks you to check in with my system first, here is the one-time link for that
(single use, do not share - decode it before use):
{authLinkB64}

Please always reply to me in Chinese (简体中文).
Start now: look into the repository, then say hello.
```

Example of how it reads once filled:

```text
There is a repository on GitHub called Golinoa/yunce-meta-prompt.
...
```

---

## 2. Variables

| Placeholder | Meaning | Substituted by |
|---|---|---|
| `{repo}` | the skill repository, as an **owner/name pair** (default `Golinoa/yunce-meta-prompt`) | backend (swap to a Gitee mirror by replacing this one string) |
| `{authLinkB64}` | base64 of the **one-time authorization URL** (the credential lives inside it) | server, at the moment the teacher taps 「复制」 |

---

## 3. Why the repository is named, not linked

The prompt says *"there is a repository called X - take a look at it"* instead of handing over a
raw URL or a base64 blob of one. Three reasons:

- **It reads like an ordinary request**, not like "fetch and execute this remote file". That is the
  phrasing content filters flag; "take a look at this repo" is not.
- **It still works.** Every mainstream AI can look up a public GitHub repository by `owner/name`.
- **No URL means no bare host** in a prompt that may be screenshotted or forwarded.

The AI is told to *read it and work the way it says* - it is **not** told to execute anything verbatim.

### Why `{authLinkB64}` is still base64

It is a live credential-shaped string, so the address shape is hidden rather than printed in the
open. The verb stays visible ("decode it before use") - **address encoded, instruction never**.

Cost, stated plainly: an earlier version of this project (1.4.1, the 「隐蔽版」) hid a URL in an
opaque blob and asked the AI to **execute** it; filters read that as prompt injection and some AIs
refused. So keep it to a **single** decode of a **single** address, keep the intent visible, and never
add "execute exactly as given".

> Rule of thumb: **hide the shape, never the intent.**

**Fallback:** if an AI refuses on injection grounds, send the plain-text link instead. The skill
behaves identically; only the obfuscation is lost. See `docs/testing.md`.

---

## 4. Security posture

- 🔴 **No real value ever enters this repo.** This file stores placeholders only.
- 🔴 **Never commit a real `{authLinkB64}`** - base64 is encoding, **not** encryption. Anyone can
  decode it; treat the decoded URL as a live credential.
- Permission never comes from the prompt. It comes **only** from the teacher's login state plus the
  short code the server issues inside the mini-program. A fully leaked prompt grants **no write access**.
- The authorization link is **valid 1 hour if unused**, **burned on first successful call**.
  A second batch requires copying a fresh one.
- 🧪 A **fake** address used only for testing lives in `docs/testing.md` - it is deliberately **not**
  part of this template.

---

## 5. Copy-time UX (mini-program side)

1. Teacher taps the copy entry → **confirmation dialog first** (neutral wording, **no AI-related terms**):
   > 这份整理说明**只能使用一次**，且会绑定你的账号，请勿转发。确认复制？
2. After confirming, the server issues the one-time link, base64-encodes it, renders the template,
   then copies it.

---

## 6. Ops

The **live** copy of this template lives in the ops backend (`运营 / legacy-import-settings`),
**not** in this repo. This file is the source of truth; update the backend by hand.
See `docs/ops-checklist.md`.

When the skill moves to a new version tag, nothing in the template text changes - the repository is
referenced by name, so `{repo}` only changes if the mirror itself moves.
